<h3 class="wp-block-heading wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__heading is-style-h2"><strong>Alberto Leoncio</strong></h3>



<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>Brazil</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">Most work on Wikipedia happens behind the scenes and is performed by volunteers like Alberto. The time Alberto spends on technical tasks makes life easier for all other Portuguese Wikipedia editors.</p>

</div>



<div class="has_overlay align wp-block-wmf-reports-marker" id="1752170660411" data-lat="28.326539837267" data-long="35.249988887993">
	

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-style-default wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="512" height="341" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/512px-Wikiar2022_0034_cropped.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-78902" style="aspect-ratio:3/2;object-fit:cover" srcset="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/512px-Wikiar2022_0034_cropped.jpg 512w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/512px-Wikiar2022_0034_cropped.jpg?resize=300,200 300w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 512px) 100vw, 512px" /></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__heading is-style-h2"><strong>Alaa Najjar</strong></h3>



<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>MENA region</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">Alaa’s nearly 600,000 edits on Wikimedia projects have expanded the sites’ knowledge of medicine, anatomy, and biology. In thanks, he received the prestigious 2021 Wikimedian of the Year award.</p>

</div>



<div class="has_overlay align wp-block-wmf-reports-marker" id="1752170660412" data-lat="9.59396" data-long="8.105306">
	

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-style-default wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1024" height="891" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Nkem_Osuigwe_3.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-78907" style="aspect-ratio:3/2;object-fit:cover" srcset="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Nkem_Osuigwe_3.jpg 1024w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Nkem_Osuigwe_3.jpg?resize=300,261 300w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Nkem_Osuigwe_3.jpg?resize=768,668 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>

<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>Nigeria</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">Nkem is a connector: she brings volunteer Wikimedia editors and librarians from Africa together. Her work in organizing the first African Librarians Week generated nearly 28,000 improvements on Wikipedia.</p>

</div>



<div class="has_overlay align wp-block-wmf-reports-marker" id="1752170660413" data-lat="22.700590656789" data-long="78.729942717069">

<h3 class="wp-block-heading wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__heading is-style-h2"><strong>Ananya Mondal</strong></h3>



<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>India</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">A clinical nutritionist by trade, Ananya singlehandedly spearheaded an initiative to upload more images of butterflies onto Wikimedia projects. She’s since inspired people to upload over 15,000 new photos.</p>

</div>



<div class="has_overlay align wp-block-wmf-reports-marker" id="1752170660414" data-lat="64.964875" data-long="17.675409">
	

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-style-default wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1024" height="682" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Netha_Hussain-070A3987.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-78916" style="aspect-ratio:3/2;object-fit:cover" srcset="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Netha_Hussain-070A3987.jpg 1024w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Netha_Hussain-070A3987.jpg?resize=300,200 300w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/1024px-Netha_Hussain-070A3987.jpg?resize=768,512 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__heading is-style-h2"><strong>Netha Hussain</strong></h3>



<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>Sweden</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">Netha uses her expertise as a doctor to ensure medical content on Wikipedia is accurate, well-sourced, and easily understood—from COVID-19 content during the pandemic to documenting misinformation around women’s health.</p>

</div>



<div class="has_overlay align wp-block-wmf-reports-marker" id="1752170660415" data-lat="39.381266" data-long="-97.922211">

<p class="wmf-pattern-reports-carousel-slide__location is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size"><em>United States</em></p>



<p class="is-style-sans-p has-medium-font-size">Rosie co-founded the Women in Red project, which is spearheading an effort to increase Wikipedia’s biographies about women in English. So far, they’ve added over 200,000 articles.</p>

Get to know us People Board of Trustees Executive team Staff Reports Annual reports Financial reports Transparency reports Careers Frequently asked questions What we do Our technology supports the backbone of knowledge on the internet. Learn more about our work Wikimedia projects Technology Public policy Closing knowledge gaps What you can do The more people take part, the better the internet’s knowledge gets. Donate Donate to help keep Wikipedia free and accessible. Become a monthly donor Ways to give Reasons to donate Leave a gift in your will Manage a recurring donation Volunteer From editing to organizing, find out how you can get involved. Advocate Help us protect Wikipedia and the people who make it possible. News Stay up to date on our efforts to protect free knowledge. Find out more Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US unionization request Search Search Search Current language: en English العربية Français Español Português Donate now We support protect fund open human knowledge We are the nonprofit that hosts Wikipedia. We support the people, technology, and policies that enable reliable information to be shared with the world. Help us support everyone’s access to reliable information. Why donate? Amount ₹ Frequency Just once Give monthly Donate now Celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th birthday Mark this milestone by paying tribute to the hundreds of thousands of people that edit, write, and fact check the backbone of knowledge on the internet. Join the party By the numbers Wikipedia is the backbone of the internet’s knowledge. From students to chatbots, everyone learns from it. Wikipedia receives nearly 15 billion views each month. The Wikimedia Foundation supports nearly 265,000 volunteers every month. Every minute 324 new edits are made to Wikipedia. With over 67 million articles , in 300+ languages , Wikipedia is the home of trusted information online. Wikipedia is the only website among the top 10 most visited that is hosted by a nonprofit organization. Our work Read more about how we are supporting the people, policies, and products that make Wikipedia and Wikimedia projects possible. Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US unionization request Community Paris hosts Wikimania 2026 as Wikipedia celebrates 25 years of free knowledge Technology The cost of ‘free’: How Wikimedia Enterprise protects Wikipedia in the AI era Public policy Wikimedia Foundation Challenges UK Online Safety Act Regulations Equity Wikimedia Foundation co-hosts second UN Open Source Week edit-a-thon Wikimedia Foundation China again blocks the Wikimedia Foundation as a permanent observer to the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Our projects African Journalists Receive ‘Open the Knowledge’ Awards from ICFJ and Wikimedia Foundation Built for people, by people Wikipedia is built by nearly 250,000 volunteers from all kinds of backgrounds. They edit articles, check facts, fix code, and help make the internet’s knowledge better. Meet some of them. Taufik Rosman Malaysia The 2023 Wikimedian of the Year, Taufik has been editing since he was 8 years old. He has expanded the Malay Wiktionary with nearly 11,000 changes. “Each of our contributions matters greatly,” Taufik says. Siobhan Leachman New Zealand Siobhan expands English Wikipedia with knowledge about notable women in biodiversity and natural history. Thanks to her, Wikipedia has information about all of New Zealand’s 1,800 endemic moth species. Armine Aghayan-Flisch Switzerland Writing a Wikipedia article each day for a hundred straight days is a feat. Arminé has done it thirteen times on the Armenian Wikipedia, while also uploading over 20,000 open-licensed images. Donatien Kangah Côte d’Ivoire The most visible part of Donatien’s French Wikipedia work is in the site’s coverage of African football. But behind the scenes, Danatien also runs an organization that expands Wikipedia’s knowledge of Côte d’Ivoire. Wilfredo Rodríguez Canada Prolific photographer Wilfredo has shared over 50,000 images with Wikimedia projects. Many come from his home country of Venezuela to preserve its beauty for the world’s benefit. Ellie Méndez El Salvador Ellie has collaborated with multiple El Salvadorean cultural institutions to expand Wikipedia’s coverage of women’s sports in Spanish and train people in updating the site. Mónica Paola Bonilla-Parra Colombia As the head of Wikimedia Colombia, Mónica works to encourage people to share knowledge on Wikipedia. “There are no limits to participating and contributing,” she says. “If you don’t do it, who will?” Alberto Leoncio Brazil Most work on Wikipedia happens behind the scenes and is performed by volunteers like Alberto. The time Alberto spends on technical tasks makes life easier for all other Portuguese Wikipedia editors. Alaa Najjar MENA region Alaa’s nearly 600,000 edits on Wikimedia projects have expanded the sites’ knowledge of medicine, anatomy, and biology. In thanks, he received the prestigious 2021 Wikimedian of the Year award. Nkem Osuigwe Nigeria Nkem is a connector: she brings volunteer Wikimedia editors and librarians from Africa together. Her work in organizing the first African Librarians Week generated nearly 28,000 improvements on Wikipedia. Ananya Mondal India A clinical nutritionist by trade, Ananya singlehandedly spearheaded an initiative to upload more images of butterflies onto Wikimedia projects. She’s since inspired people to upload over 15,000 new photos. Netha Hussain Sweden Netha uses her expertise as a doctor to ensure medical content on Wikipedia is accurate, well-sourced, and easily understood—from COVID-19 content during the pandemic to documenting misinformation around women’s health. Rosie Stephenson-Goodknight United States Rosie co-founded the Women in Red project, which is spearheading an effort to increase Wikipedia’s biographies about women in English. So far, they’ve added over 200,000 articles. Andrew Lih United States Long-time Wikipedian Andrew wrote The Wikipedia Revolution, a foundational book on the history of Wikipedia. Over the last two decades, he’s made over 760,000 improvements across Wikimedia projects. <h1 class="wp-block-heading">What we do</h1>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-display-font-family" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:400">We help everyone share in the sum of all knowledge.</h3>
</div>



<div class="wp-block-column is-layout-flow wp-block-column-is-layout-flow">
<figure class="wp-block-image aligncenter size-large is-resized has-custom-border"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/KS_edit-a-thon_2017-02-a_jeh-e1533254882601.jpg?w=1024" alt="Art+Feminism Wikipedia edit-a-thon" class="wp-image-285" style="border-radius:4px;aspect-ratio:1.5;object-fit:cover;width:452px;height:auto" srcset="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/KS_edit-a-thon_2017-02-a_jeh-e1533254882601.jpg 1024w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/KS_edit-a-thon_2017-02-a_jeh-e1533254882601.jpg?resize=300,200 300w, https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/KS_edit-a-thon_2017-02-a_jeh-e1533254882601.jpg?resize=768,512 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>



<div class="wp-block-group alignwide is-layout-flow wp-block-group-is-layout-flow">
<p>We are the people who keep knowledge free. There is an amazing community of people around the world that makes great projects like Wikipedia. We help them do that work. We take care of the technical infrastructure, the legal challenges, and the growing pains.</p>
</div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stairs">
<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Host free knowledge projects</h2><img decoding="async" class="wp-image-61198 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Wikimedia_Foundation_Servers_2015-63-e1565971769756.jpg?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body">The Wikimedia Foundation was established as a nonprofit in 2003 to give Wikipedia a permanent home. We now <a href="/what-we-do/wikimedia-projects/">host 13 collaborative free knowledge projects</a>, from <a href="/our-work/wikipedia/">Wikipedia</a>, the free encyclopedia, to <a href="/our-work/wikidata/">Wikidata</a>, a set of structured data, and more. We maintain the servers, build the software, and design the technology that keep these projects running.</p></div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Deliver grants for good</h2><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="wp-image-61195 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Skrivstuga_ArtAndFeminism_Stockholm_09-e1565971792652.jpg?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body">We partner with Wikimedia communities around the world to provide them with the support they need to do great work. Last year we awarded over 9 million USD in grants to Wikimedia community members, affiliates and nonprofit organizations. <a href="https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Grants:Start">We fund</a> editathons, outreach efforts, events, and conferences. We help them get the word out for free knowledge.</p></div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Grow community around the world</h2><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="wp-image-61197 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Wikimania_2016_-_group_photo_02-e1565971776858.jpg?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body">When more people can access and contribute to free knowledge, the better that knowledge reflects the world. We are committed to helping grow and sustain a healthy community of over 265,000 people across 170 nations. From the <a href="https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Community_health_initiative">community health initiative</a> to <a href="/2015/11/30/artificial-intelligence-x-ray-specs/">ORES</a> and <a href="/our-work/project-rewrite/">our work in gender diversity</a>, the Foundation is actively working to make our projects more inclusive.</p></div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Support education and learning worldwide</h2><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="wp-image-63085 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Club_de_Edición_II_mayo_2017.jpg?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body">We help teachers and students of all ages access and use the full potential of Wikimedia projects for their learning objectives. Key pillars of our education work include promoting knowledge equity and teaching 21st century skills.</p></div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Partner for change</h2><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="wp-image-74697 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1024px-Oxford_-_Oxford_University_Museum_of_Natural_History_-_0247.jpg?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body">Working with partners like Google, the <a href="https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity_Heritage_Library" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Biodiversity Heritage Library</a>, and <a href="https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/unesco-joins-2023-wikimedia-movement-singapore" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">UNESCO</a>, Wikimedia actively seeks new knowledge, closing systemic gaps in global understanding of science, culture, language, and identity. <a href="https://wikimediafoundation.org/the-wikipedia-library/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Wikipedia Library</a> partners the world’s top publishers with Wikipedia.</p></div>



<div class="wp-block-shiro-stair stair"><h2 class="stair__heading is-style-h3">Open the Knowledge</h2><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="wp-image-65288 size-image_16x9_small stair__image" src="https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/DEI_Representation.png?w=600&h=338&crop=1" height="338" width="600"/><p class="stair__body"><a href="https://wikimediafoundation.org/about/open-the-knowledge/">“Open the Knowledge”</a> is our call to everyone to promote radical knowledge equity, creating a living record of history, stories, and contexts for and by all people. It aims to make the Wikimedia movement more diverse, equitable, and inclusive.</p></div>
</div>

https://wikimediafoundation.org/what-we-.visible_text: --> What we do – Wikimedia Foundation Skip to content Who we are We are the non-profit organization behind Wikipedia. Get to know us People Board of Trustees Executive team Staff Reports Annual reports Financial reports Transparency reports Careers Frequently asked questions What we do Our technology supports the backbone of knowledge on the internet. Learn more about our work Wikimedia projects Technology Public policy Closing knowledge gaps What you can do The more people take part, the better the internet’s knowledge gets. Donate Donate to help keep Wikipedia free and accessible. Become a monthly donor Ways to give Reasons to donate Leave a gift in your will Manage a recurring donation Volunteer From editing to organizing, find out how you can get involved. Advocate Help us protect Wikipedia and the people who make it possible. News Stay up to date on our efforts to protect free knowledge. Find out more Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US unionization request Search Search Search Current language: en English العربية Français Español Português Donate now You are here: Home What we do What we do What we do We help everyone share in the sum of all knowledge. We are the people who keep knowledge free. There is an amazing community of people around the world that makes great projects like Wikipedia. We help them do that work. We take care of the technical infrastructure, the legal challenges, and the growing pains. Host free knowledge projects The Wikimedia Foundation was established as a nonprofit in 2003 to give Wikipedia a permanent home. We now host 13 collaborative free knowledge projects , from Wikipedia , the free encyclopedia, to Wikidata , a set of structured data, and more. We maintain the servers, build the software, and design the technology that keep these projects running. Deliver grants for good We partner with Wikimedia communities around the world to provide them with the support they need to do great work. Last year we awarded over 9 million USD in grants to Wikimedia community members, affiliates and nonprofit organizations.  We fund  editathons, outreach efforts, events, and conferences. We help them get the word out for free knowledge. Grow community around the world When more people can access and contribute to free knowledge, the better that knowledge reflects the world. We are committed to helping grow and sustain a healthy community of over 265,000 people across 170 nations. From the  community health initiative  to  ORES  and  our work in gender diversity , the Foundation is actively working to make our projects more inclusive. Support education and learning worldwide We help teachers and students of all ages access and use the full potential of Wikimedia projects for their learning objectives. Key pillars of our education work include promoting knowledge equity and teaching 21st century skills. Partner for change Working with partners like Google, the Biodiversity Heritage Library , and UNESCO , Wikimedia actively seeks new knowledge, closing systemic gaps in global understanding of science, culture, language, and identity. The Wikipedia Library partners the world’s top publishers with Wikipedia. Open the Knowledge “Open the Knowledge” is our call to everyone to promote radical knowledge equity, creating a living record of history, stories, and contexts for and by all people. It aims to make the Wikimedia movement more diverse, equitable, and inclusive. See what we have been up to Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Today, eligible Wikimedia Foundation staff in the United States voted in favor of union representation. The election was conducted by the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) by secret ballot. 3 September 2026 By Wikimedia Foundation Read more Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation The Wikimedia Foundation, the global nonprofit that operates Wikipedia, today announced the appointment of Rena Kokalari as its new Chief People Officer. 4 August 2026 By Wikimedia Foundation Read more Help expand human knowledge There are many different ways for you to support us. Here are some ideas for putting your skills and passions to use: Donate Join the readers who help fund Wikipedia Edit Join the community that builds Wikipedia Participate From coding to photography to organizing events, contribute your skills to advance free knowledge Advocate Help us protect everyone’s right to knowledge Subscribe for news Get the latest updates about the Wikimedia Foundation directly to your inbox. Email Address * Confirm choice * Yes, I would like to receive updates, news, and promotional emails from the Wikimedia Foundation. I understand I can unsubscribe at any time. * = required field Alternative Email: For more details, see our Privacy statement. Get to know us People Board of Trustees Executive team Staff Reports Annual reports Financial reports Transparency reports Careers Frequently asked questions What we do Our technology supports the backbone of knowledge on the internet. Learn more about our work Wikimedia projects Technology Public policy Closing knowledge gaps What you can do The more people take part, the better the internet’s knowledge gets. Donate Donate to help keep Wikipedia free and accessible. Become a monthly donor Ways to give Reasons to donate Leave a gift in your will Manage a recurring donation Volunteer From editing to organizing, find out how you can get involved. Advocate Help us protect Wikipedia and the people who make it possible. News Stay up to date on our efforts to protect free knowledge. Find out more Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US unionization request Search Search Search Current language: en English العربية Français Español Português Donate now You are here: Home Contact Contact This page contains contact information for specific individuals and functions related to the Wikimedia movement. If you are interested in general discussion about Wikimedia and its projects with the community, please join one of our public mailing lists or IRC channels . Email addresses Questions related to Wikipedia or other wikis (Wikimedia projects): info@wikimedia.org Questions related to donations: donate@wikimedia.org Disclaimer: Due to the volume of inquiries we receive, we use  Zendesk  as a donor response platform. By emailing  donate@wikimedia.org , you understand that your information will be processed by the Zendesk Group in accordance with Zendesk’s  terms . Users from the following countries should consult Section 13 of Zendesk’s  privacy policy  for more information about Zendesk’s country-specific practices: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Singapore. Questions related to partnerships: business@wikimedia.org Press and media contacts: Please visit our press room . Other questions for and about the Wikimedia Foundation: answers@wikimedia.org Disclaimer: Emails to info@wikimedia.org are reviewed and responded to by volunteers from our user community. Please understand that the Wikimedia Foundation cannot guarantee confidential treatment of any sensitive information you include in your message. Postal address Wikimedia Foundation, Inc. 1 Sansome Street Suite 1895 San Francisco, California 94104 USA Phone: +1-415-839-6885 Fax: +1-415-347-8540 Please do not send legal documents to this address, for Legal Service of Process, see below . Please note: We receive a large number of calls, so email or fax is always a better first option. If you leave a voicemail, please include an email address for faster response. Before contacting us, please review Answers on Meta-Wiki to best direct your inquiry. Address for donations Wikimedia Foundation, Inc. P.O. Box 98204 Washington, DC 20090-8204 USA Please note: donations by check are processed directly at our centralized lockbox location, which is in Washington, DC. Legal Copyright violations If you would like to send us a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (“DMCA”) takedown notice or counter-notice regarding a potential copyright violation, you can find more information, and where to send your request, on our DMCA takedowns page . Requests to disclose user information (including emergency requests) Please read our Requests for User Information Procedures and Guidelines and then send your request to: Wikimedia Foundation c/o CT Corporation System 330 North Brand Boulevard Glendale, California 91203-2336 legal@wikimedia.org Other legal questions or requests Please send all other legal questions or requests to: Wikimedia Foundation c/o CT Corporation System 330 North Brand Boulevard Glendale, California 91203-2336 legal@wikimedia.org Wikimedia movement affiliates Wikimedia movement affiliates support work focused on a specific theme, topic, or subject within or across countries and regions. https://wikimediafoundation.org/ar/.visible_text: --> الرئيسية – مؤسسة ويكيميديا تخطى الى المحتوى من نحن نحن المنظمة غير الربحية التي تقف وراء ويكيبيديا. تعرّف علينا الكوادر البشرية مجلس الأمناء الفريق التنفيذي الموظفون التقارير التقارير السنوية التقارير المالية تقارير الشفافية الوظائف الأسئلة الشائعة أعمالنا تُسهم تقنيتنا في دعم البنية الأساسية للمعرفة على الإنترنت تعرّف أكثر على أعمالنا مشاريع ويكيميديا التقنية السياسات العامة سد الفجوة المعرفية ما الذي يمكنك فعله كلما زاد عدد المشاركين، أصبحت المعرفة على الإنترنت أفضل. التبرّع تبرّع للمساهمة في إبقاء ويكيبيديا مجانية ومتاحة للجميع كن متبرعاً شهرياً طرق العطاء أسباب التبرع خصص هدية في وصيتك فكّر في تعزيز تبرعك الدوري التطوّع من التحرير إلى التنظيم، اكتشف كيف يمكنك المساهمة. المناصرة ساعدنا في حماية ويكيبيديا والأشخاص الذين يقفون خلف نجاحها الأخبار تابع آخر المستجدات حول الجهود التي نبذلها لحماية المعرفة الحرة. اكتشف المزيد مشاريعنا ويكيبيديا تحتفل بمرور 25 عاماً على المعرفة في أبهى صورها مؤسسة ويكيميديا كيف تستخدم مؤسسة ويكيميديا ​​التبرعات المقدمة إلى ويكيبيديا؟ مؤسسة ويكيميديا , مشاريعنا كيف تُموّل ويكيبيديا؟ بحث بحث بحث اللغة الحالية: ar العربية English Français Español Português تبرع الأن نحن ندعم نحمي نموّل نفتح المعرفة البشرية نحن المنظمة غير الربحية التي تستضيف ويكيبيديا. نحن ندعم الأشخاص، والتكنولوجيا، والسياسات التي تُمكّن وتتيح مشاركة المعلومات الموثوقة مع العالم. ساهم في دعم وصول الجميع إلى المعلومات الموثوقة. لماذا تتبرع؟ المبلغ ₹ التكرار مرة واحدة فقط التبرع شهريًا تبرع الآن نحتفل بذكرى ميلاد ويكيبيديا الخامس والعشرين لنخلّد هذه المرحلة الفارقة بالاحتفاء بمئات آلاف الأشخاص الذين يساهمون تحريراً وكتابةً وتدقيقاً لتكوين وبناء هذه الموسوعة التي تشكّل العمود الفقري للمعرفة على الإنترنت شارك في الحفل حقائق الأرقام تعتبر ويكيبيديا العمود الفقري للمعرفة على الإنترنت. من الطلاب إلى روبوتات المحادثة، الجميع يتعلم منها. تحقق ويكيبيديا أكثر من 15 مليار مشاهدةٍ شهرياً. تدعم مؤسسة ويكيميديا قرابة 265,000 متطوع شهرياً. يُضاف إلى ويكيبيديا قرابة 324 تعديلاً جديداً كل دقيقة. بوجود أكثر من 67 مليون مقالة ، بأكثر من 300 لغة ، تعتبر ويكيبيديا موطناً للمعلومات الموثوقة على الإنترنت. ويكيبيديا هي الموقع الوحيد من بين المواقع العشرة الأكثر زيارة في العالم الذي تستضيفه منظمة غير ربحية. عملنا تعرّف المزيد عن كيفية دعمنا للأشخاص، والسياسات، والمنتجات التي تجعل من ويكيبيديا ومشاريع ويكيميديا ممكنة. مشاريعنا ويكيبيديا تحتفل بمرور 25 عاماً على المعرفة في أبهى صورها مؤسسة ويكيميديا كيف تستخدم مؤسسة ويكيميديا ​​التبرعات المقدمة إلى ويكيبيديا؟ مؤسسة ويكيميديا , مشاريعنا كيف تُموّل ويكيبيديا؟ مشاريعنا في عصر الذكاء الاصطناعي، أصبحت ويكيبيديا أكثر قيمة من أي وقت مضى مؤسسة ويكيميديا هل تحبون ويكيبيديا؟ تعرّفوا على المنظمة غير الربحية التي تقف وراءها مؤسسة ويكيميديا الحفاظ على موثوقية المعلومات في العصر الرقمي: دروس مستفادة من ويكيبيديا بُنيت من أجل البشر، بأيدي البشر بُنيت ويكيبيديا على أيدي ما يقرب من 250,000 متطوع من خلفيات متنوعة. يقومون بتحرير المقالات، والتحقق من الحقائق، وإصلاح الأكواد والشيفرات، والمساعدة في تحسين معرفة الإنترنت. تعرّف على بعضهم. توفيق روسمان ماليزيا توفيق، الحائز على لقب ويكيميدي العام 2023، يحرّر منذ أن كان في الثامنة من عمره. وقد رَفدَ موسوعة ويكيبيديا الماليزية بما يقارب 11,000 تعديل. يقول توفيق: “كل مساهمة نقدّمها تُحدث فرقاً كبيراً”. شيوفان ليتشمان نيوزيلندا تضيف شيوفان إلى موسوعة ويكيبيديا الإنجليزية معلومات عن نساء بارزات في مجال التنوع البيولوجي والتاريخ الطبيعي. بفضلها، تحتوي ويكيبيديا على معلومات عن جميع أنواع العثّ المتوطنة في نيوزيلندا، والبالغ عددها 1800 نوع. أرمينيه أغايان-فليتش سويسرا كتابة مقالة واحدة في ويكيبيديا يومياً لمدة مئة يوم متتالية إنجاز بحد ذاته، وقد حققت أرمينيه هذا التحدي ثلاث عشرة مرة في ويكيبيديا الأرمينية، فضلاً عن إضافة أكثر من 20,000 صورة مرخّصة برخصة حرة. دوناتيان كانغاه ساحل العاج الجانب الأبرز في مساهمات دوناتيان في ويكيبيديا الفرنسية يتركز في تغطية كرة القدم الإفريقية. لكن خلف الكواليس، يدير دوناتيان أيضاً منظمةً تُعنى بتوسيع محتوى ويكيبيديا المعرفي عن ساحل العاج. ويلفريدو رودريغيز كندا قدّم المصور المبدع ذو الإنتاج الغزير ويلفريدو أكثر من 50,000 صورة لمشاريع ويكيميديا، كثير منها يوثّق جمال بلده فنزويلا، ليحفظه ويشاركه مع العالم.” إيلي منديز السلفادور تعاونت إيلي مع العديد من المؤسسات الثقافية السلفادورية لتوسيع محتوى ويكيبيديا المتعلق بالرياضات النسائية باللغة الإسبانية وتدريب الأشخاص على تحديث الموقع. مونيكا باولا بونيّا-بارّا كولومبيا بصفتها رئيسة ويكيميديا ​​كولومبيا، لا تتوانى مونيكا عن تشجيع الناس على مشاركة المعرفة على ويكيبيديا. وتفيد بهذا الخصوص: “لا حدود للمشاركة والمساهمة. إن لم تفعلوا ذلك، فمن سيفعل؟” ألبرتو ليونسيو البرازيل معظم العمل في ويكيبيديا يجري خلف الكواليس، وينفّذه متطوعون مثل ألبرتو. تُسهّل الجهود التي يبذلها ألبرتو لإنجاز المهام التقنية الأمورَ على جميع محرري ويكيبيديا باللغة البرتغالية. علاء النجار منطقة الشرق الأوسط ساهمت تعديلات علاء، التي تجاوزت 600,000 تعديل في مشاريع ويكيميديا، بتوسيع نطاق المعرفة في الطب والتشريح والأحياء. وتقديراً لمساهماته القيّمة، مُنح علاء جائزة ويكيميدي العام ​​المرموقة لعام 2021. نكيم أوسويغوي نيجيريا نكيم عنصر وصل فعّال؛ فهي تجمع بين محرري ويكيميديا المتطوعين وأمناء المكتبات من إفريقيا. وقد أثمرت جهودها في تنظيم أول أسبوع لأمناء مكتبات إفريقيا عن إنجاز قرابة 28,000 تعديل في ويكيبيديا أنانيا موندال الهند أنانيا موندال، أخصائية تغذية سريرية، أطلقت بمفردها مبادرة تهدف إلى رفع المزيد من صور الفراشات في مشاريع ويكيميديا. ومنذ ذلك الحين، ألهمت الآخرين للمساهمة بأكثر من 15,000 صورة جديدة. نيثا حسين السويد تستثمر نيثا خبرتها بصفتها طبيبة لضمان دقّة وموثوقية وسهولة فهم المعلومات الطبية في ويكيبيديا – بدءًا من محتوى كوفيد-19 أثناء الجائحة إلى توثيق المعلومات المغلوطة المتعلقة بصحة النساء. روزي ستيفنسون-غود نايت الولايات المتحدة شاركت روزي بتأسيس مشروع “نساء باللون الأحمر”، الذي يقود جهوداً لزيادة عدد السير الذاتية للنساء في ويكيبيديا الإنجليزية. حتى الآن، أضاف المشروع أكثر من 200,000 مقالة. أندرو ليه الولايات المتحدة أندرو ليه ويكيبيدي مخضرم، ألّف كتاب “ثورة ويكيبيديا”، وهو كتاب تأسيسي عن تاريخ ويكيبيديا. على مدى العقدين الماضيين، أجرى أندرو أكثر من 760,000 تحسيناً في مشاريع ويكيميديا. 	<h1></h1>
</div>


</div>

			<div class="article-title">
			<p><em>Five years in, <a href="http://enterprise.wikimedia.com" rel="noreferrer noopener">Wikimedia Enterprise</a> is one of the ways we get AI and big tech to stop putting strain on the free and open web</em>.</p>		</div>
	
	<article class="wysiwyg alignfull is-layout-constrained has-global-padding">
		


<p>The digital commons are under threat: with the advent of generative AI, bots have officially <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/26/ai-bots-humans-internet.html#:~:text=AI%20and%20bots%20have%20officially%20taken%20over%20the%20internet%2C%20report%20finds" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">surpassed human traffic on the internet</a>. Last year, the Wikimedia Foundation shared our concerns around <a href="https://wikimediafoundation.org/news/2025/10/17/new-user-trends-on-wikipedia/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">drops in human traffic</a> on Wikipedia. We also <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2025/04/01/how-crawlers-impact-the-operations-of-the-wikimedia-projects/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">reported a significant increase in bot traffic</a> to Wikimedia projects — largely coming from crawlers that extract content to train generative AI systems. Wikimedia projects such as Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wikimedia Commons have been obvious choices for training: they are among the last bastions of high-quality, human-created and curated content. However, the resulting strain on our infrastructure and risk of impact on our user experience requires us to respond to this threat to continue our mission of making knowledge freely accessible to everyone, everywhere. </p>



<p>As the Wikimedia Foundation continues to take <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2026/03/26/quo-vadis-crawlers-progress-and-whats-next-on-safeguarding-our-infrastructure/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">steady steps to protect its infrastructure</a>, a big part of creating a sustainable solution for our knowledge mission is <a href="https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Wikimedia Enterprise</a>, a commercial service and product we started working on five years ago.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Building Wikimedia Enterprise</h2>



<p>Though it’s become <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2025/04/01/how-crawlers-impact-the-operations-of-the-wikimedia-projects/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">a more significant concern in the AI era</a>, commercial reuse of Wikimedia data taxing our servers has been a problem for some time. For over a decade already, Wikimedia content has been crawled to power commercial products like search engines, voice assistants, knowledge panels, and any other service that needs up-to-date information about the world.</p>



<p><strong>But while our content is free, our infrastructure is not.</strong> The companies running these services weren’t the ones paying for the maintenance and upkeep of the servers they were accessing to get our content. Our individual donors were the ones footing the bill. <strong>The Foundation needed to find a way to get those commercial institutions profiting off the digital commons to help carry the burden of sustaining those commons.</strong></p>



<p>Did we think this approach would be easy? Not in the slightest. <strong>Nobody wants to pay for something when you’re already giving it to them for free</strong>. Still, we made a bet that if Wikimedia Enterprise could provide a comprehensive product experience that catered to their business needs of scale and speed with new features and functionality they want, reusers would be more easily drawn to make the switch.</p>



<p>The Wikimedia Enterprise team talked to big tech companies and other commercial reusers to find out <a href="https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/blog/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">how they were using Wikimedia projects in their products</a>. <strong>Then we set out to build a product geared towards their use cases</strong>: a set of APIs for high-volume, high-frequency access that integrated and normalized the Wikimedia projects’ many datasets into a unified offering with a well-structured, extensible data schema.</p>



<p><strong>Wikimedia Enterprise’s commercial strategy isn’t licensing-based. It’s access-based.</strong> The content of Wikimedia projects will forever be free and open to anyone. But Wikimedia Enterprise shines when you need access to that data at the volumes that automated scrapers and commercial businesses need: it offers automated bulk and real-time access to Wikimedia’s vast and constantly updated store of knowledge, packaged in a product designed to seamlessly support a wide range of commercial use cases.</p>



<p>Five years since the launch of Wikimedia Enterprise, we can safely say: <strong>it’s working.</strong> Since its inception, <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2025/11/24/wikimedia-enterprise-financial-report-fiscal-year-2024-2025/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Wikimedia Enterprise has fully repaid its initial investment and is now contributing back to the Wikimedia Foundation’s long-term sustainability</a>. We did this by iterating the product offering and creating incentives for commercial organizations to switch to Wikimedia Enterprise’s infrastructure, all without sacrificing the broader goal of keeping the Wikimedia projects free for human users and mission-aligned partners and communities. <strong>Income from Wikimedia Enterprise is capped at 30% of the total Wikimedia Foundation annual revenue.</strong> This cap was established in order to ensure that the majority of funding continues to come from small donations from millions of readers – a key ingredient to ensuring Wikimedia’s ongoing independence. This has allowed the Wikimedia Foundation to continue serving its mission of preserving the open knowledge ecosystem, while forging meaningful partnerships with tech companies and other commercial businesses so that they can do their part to sustain and preserve the ecosystem as well. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Establishing boundaries for commercial reuse</h2>



<p>Building the infrastructure of Wikimedia Enterprise and creating incentives for commercial organizations to switch to it is not enough. <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2026/03/26/quo-vadis-crawlers-progress-and-whats-next-on-safeguarding-our-infrastructure/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bad-faith actors continue to tax our public API infrastructure</a> to crawl and scrape, spoofing their identities, using residential proxies, and more. This has put multiple kinds of increased pressure on the Wikimedia Foundation’s limited resources as a non-profit — and ultimately impacts the knowledge commons that the world relies on. </p>



<p>To ensure commercial reusers know they need to switch to Wikimedia Enterprise, we have to use new tactics. We’re not switching off our existing public API access, now or ever, but we have begun <strong>rate-limiting large-scale reusers of the Wikimedia Foundation public APIs.</strong> If a company needs to access our data at a significant enough speed or volume, Wikimedia Enterprise is now the right place for them to go — a must-do rather than a nice-to-have. This rate-limiting is a difficult balancing act of protecting our infrastructure while fostering our community. It’s not easy, <a href="https://diff.wikimedia.org/2026/03/26/quo-vadis-crawlers-progress-and-whats-next-on-safeguarding-our-infrastructure/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">but we’re working on viable solutions that align with our community needs</a>.</p>



<p>We’re also continuing to build out the Wikimedia Enterprise platform to make it more valuable to non-commercial reusers who aren’t profiting off Wikimedia data but still need access at scale. <strong>We’re actively </strong><a href="https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Enterprise#Exceptional_access" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>forging partnerships with non-profits and startups</strong></a> that align with the Wikimedia Foundation’s goals or values to give them free access to the Wikimedia Enterprise APIs. Volunteers can get access to Wikimedia Enterprise through <a href="https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Help:Cloud_Services_Introduction" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Wikimedia Cloud Services</a>, and we introduced <a href="https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/pricing/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">free access</a> for smaller commercial reusers as well.</p>



<p>The Wikimedia Foundation operates within many systems that make the world function. Five years ago, we started Wikimedia Enterprise to translate between the non-profit system of the Wikimedia Foundation and the for-profit system of commercial businesses, so they have an easier pathway to reuse one of the largest high-quality, human-created knowledge resources on the internet. We told them that Wikimedia projects are so valuable that we made them free for the millions of humans who rely on them every day – but, as companies building products based on these vast knowledge commons, we need you to pay for the value you derive from them so we can keep them free forever. </p>

Jolan Wuyts, Senior Technical Writer at Wikimedia Enterprise, also contributed to this post.</em></p>

Find out more Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US staff unionization Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation welcomes Rena Kokalari as new Chief People Officer Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Foundation Statement on US unionization request Search Search Search Donate now You are here: Home News The cost of ‘free’: How Wikimedia Enterprise protects Wikipedia in the AI era The cost of ‘free’: How Wikimedia Enterprise protects Wikipedia in the AI era By Lane Becker • 16 July 2026 Share Facebook Bluesky LinkedIn Email Copy Link Link copied Five years in, Wikimedia Enterprise is one of the ways we get AI and big tech to stop putting strain on the free and open web . The digital commons are under threat: with the advent of generative AI, bots have officially surpassed human traffic on the internet . Last year, the Wikimedia Foundation shared our concerns around drops in human traffic on Wikipedia. We also reported a significant increase in bot traffic to Wikimedia projects — largely coming from crawlers that extract content to train generative AI systems. Wikimedia projects such as Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wikimedia Commons have been obvious choices for training: they are among the last bastions of high-quality, human-created and curated content. However, the resulting strain on our infrastructure and risk of impact on our user experience requires us to respond to this threat to continue our mission of making knowledge freely accessible to everyone, everywhere. As the Wikimedia Foundation continues to take steady steps to protect its infrastructure , a big part of creating a sustainable solution for our knowledge mission is Wikimedia Enterprise , a commercial service and product we started working on five years ago. Building Wikimedia Enterprise Though it’s become a more significant concern in the AI era , commercial reuse of Wikimedia data taxing our servers has been a problem for some time. For over a decade already, Wikimedia content has been crawled to power commercial products like search engines, voice assistants, knowledge panels, and any other service that needs up-to-date information about the world. But while our content is free, our infrastructure is not. The companies running these services weren’t the ones paying for the maintenance and upkeep of the servers they were accessing to get our content. Our individual donors were the ones footing the bill. The Foundation needed to find a way to get those commercial institutions profiting off the digital commons to help carry the burden of sustaining those commons. Did we think this approach would be easy? Not in the slightest. Nobody wants to pay for something when you’re already giving it to them for free . Still, we made a bet that if Wikimedia Enterprise could provide a comprehensive product experience that catered to their business needs of scale and speed with new features and functionality they want, reusers would be more easily drawn to make the switch. The Wikimedia Enterprise team talked to big tech companies and other commercial reusers to find out how they were using Wikimedia projects in their products . Then we set out to build a product geared towards their use cases : a set of APIs for high-volume, high-frequency access that integrated and normalized the Wikimedia projects’ many datasets into a unified offering with a well-structured, extensible data schema. Wikimedia Enterprise’s commercial strategy isn’t licensing-based. It’s access-based. The content of Wikimedia projects will forever be free and open to anyone. But Wikimedia Enterprise shines when you need access to that data at the volumes that automated scrapers and commercial businesses need: it offers automated bulk and real-time access to Wikimedia’s vast and constantly updated store of knowledge, packaged in a product designed to seamlessly support a wide range of commercial use cases. Five years since the launch of Wikimedia Enterprise, we can safely say: it’s working. Since its inception, Wikimedia Enterprise has fully repaid its initial investment and is now contributing back to the Wikimedia Foundation’s long-term sustainability . We did this by iterating the product offering and creating incentives for commercial organizations to switch to Wikimedia Enterprise’s infrastructure, all without sacrificing the broader goal of keeping the Wikimedia projects free for human users and mission-aligned partners and communities. Income from Wikimedia Enterprise is capped at 30% of the total Wikimedia Foundation annual revenue. This cap was established in order to ensure that the majority of funding continues to come from small donations from millions of readers – a key ingredient to ensuring Wikimedia’s ongoing independence. This has allowed the Wikimedia Foundation to continue serving its mission of preserving the open knowledge ecosystem, while forging meaningful partnerships with tech companies and other commercial businesses so that they can do their part to sustain and preserve the ecosystem as well. Establishing boundaries for commercial reuse Building the infrastructure of Wikimedia Enterprise and creating incentives for commercial organizations to switch to it is not enough. Bad-faith actors continue to tax our public API infrastructure to crawl and scrape, spoofing their identities, using residential proxies, and more. This has put multiple kinds of increased pressure on the Wikimedia Foundation’s limited resources as a non-profit — and ultimately impacts the knowledge commons that the world relies on. To ensure commercial reusers know they need to switch to Wikimedia Enterprise, we have to use new tactics. We’re not switching off our existing public API access, now or ever, but we have begun rate-limiting large-scale reusers of the Wikimedia Foundation public APIs. If a company needs to access our data at a significant enough speed or volume, Wikimedia Enterprise is now the right place for them to go — a must-do rather than a nice-to-have. This rate-limiting is a difficult balancing act of protecting our infrastructure while fostering our community. It’s not easy, but we’re working on viable solutions that align with our community needs . We’re also continuing to build out the Wikimedia Enterprise platform to make it more valuable to non-commercial reusers who aren’t profiting off Wikimedia data but still need access at scale. We’re actively forging partnerships with non-profits and startups that align with the Wikimedia Foundation’s goals or values to give them free access to the Wikimedia Enterprise APIs. Volunteers can get access to Wikimedia Enterprise through Wikimedia Cloud Services , and we introduced free access for smaller commercial reusers as well. The Wikimedia Foundation operates within many systems that make the world function. Five years ago, we started Wikimedia Enterprise to translate between the non-profit system of the Wikimedia Foundation and the for-profit system of commercial businesses, so they have an easier pathway to reuse one of the largest high-quality, human-created knowledge resources on the internet. We told them that Wikimedia projects are so valuable that we made them free for the millions of humans who rely on them every day – but, as companies building products based on these vast knowledge commons, we need you to pay for the value you derive from them so we can keep them free forever.  Lane Becker is President of Wikimedia Enterprise and Senior Director of Commercial Partnerships). Jolan Wuyts, Senior Technical Writer at Wikimedia Enterprise, also contributed to this post.
